# Private security fork

This is **not an upstream patched release**. It is a private, MIT-licensed project fork of picomatch 4.0.7 for CVE-2026-112366 / GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf. `PROVENANCE.json` records the verified official npm tarball integrity, original file hashes and exact patched file hashes. The original license remains in `LICENSE`.

The upstream repeated-extglob guard skips single branches such as `+(*)` and `+(*a)`. Checking individual bodies also misses ambiguity between adjacent repeats. This private fork **rejects `+(` and `*(` syntax with a SyntaxError before aliases or fast paths**, regardless of options, including escaped occurrences and `noext`/`noextglob`. It does not silently literalize unsupported exclusion patterns, which could broaden inclusion. Parser `regex:false` is forced even if a caller requests `regex:true`, preventing raw trailing plus characters from reconstructing the vulnerable repetition. Glob pattern length is bounded to 4096 characters, including fast paths. Standard globstars, braces, non-repeated extglobs and scanning remain supported; project Jest selectors use finite `@(spec|test)` alternation. This is deliberately a narrower contract than upstream Bash matching.

**Trust boundary:** this resolved package is a development/build dependency used with repository-owned patterns, not a matcher for user-supplied glob/regex input. This patch addresses the recorded repeated-extglob advisory; it is not a general non-backtracking engine. Complex ordinary glob composition can still be costly (for example many adjacent `@(*)` groups). Do not expose arbitrary untrusted patterns through this fork, and do not claim unrestricted glob ReDoS freedom. Full application tests/build/browser checks remain required for compatibility.

The existing `npm audit --audit-level=high` remains unchanged. A separate mandatory gate verifies vendored/resolved bytes, runs public-interface timeout and compatibility regressions, and audits the original 4.0.7 registry version. The known upstream advisory is recorded as fixed **only** when the patched bytes and regression checks succeed; any additional upstream advisory fails the gate. This prevents a local fork identity from silently hiding future upstream findings.

Do not remove this gate or relabel an unpatched upstream version as safe. Replace the fork with an official release when one is available, after reviewing the patch and rerunning the same regressions and full application checks. No package is published to npm by this repository.
